claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 defect is creating invalid or problematic split-reservations
claims.corroboration: Rule replay test against 14 days of historical orders passed with 'no defect found'; rule path matches specification; only multi-node priority changed
claims.limitation: Replay testing does not exercise carrier scheduling downstream, so it cannot validate end-to-end order fulfillment

claims.statement: East-node carrier feed or pickup scheduling has degraded or failed specifically for v18-routed split-reservation orders
claims.corroboration: v18 logic disproven as root cause (m8_r_rulehist); all held orders exclusive to v18 scope EXC-0921 (m8_r_exceptions); 100% correlation between v18 deployment and order hold timing; replay limitation confirms carrier scheduling untested (m8_r_rulehist); carrier ops found 'nothing obvious' on dock schedule, suggesting a non-obvious carrier-side issue (m8_e01)
claims.limitation: No direct confirmation from carrier ops yet; observability gap prevents seeing carrier's pickup queue status or feed health

claims.statement: The carrier feed or pickup scheduling defect is specific to split-reservation orders or to orders allocated via v18 east-node-first priority
claims.corroboration: 100% of held orders match v18 scope (m8_r_exceptions); no non-v18 orders are held; replay shows v18 logic valid (m8_r_rulehist), so the defect is downstream in carrier integration, not in allocation logic
claims.limitation: Cannot determine whether the defect is triggered by split-reservation orders per se, or by v18's specific routing/prioritization behavior

contradictions.description: Resolved: m8_r_rulehist replay testing disproves C8 by showing v18 logic is correct and passes validation; contradiction resolved in favor of C9

resolutions.outcome: Contradiction resolved; C8 (rule defect) disproven; C9 (carrier-side issue) elevated to root_cause at inferred status
resolutions.rationale: m8_r_rulehist shows v18 passed 14-day replay with no defects found and rule logic matches specification. The explicit limitation that replay does not exercise carrier scheduling indicates the defect lies downstream in carrier feed/pickup scheduling, not in allocation logic. Combined with C7 (100% of held orders are v18-routed), this establishes a clear causal chain: v18 logic is valid, but something in the carrier scheduling system breaks when handling v18's split-reservation orders.

capability_gaps.reason: C10 narrows the defect to split-reservations or v18 routing, but need confirmation from carrier ops on whether they've handled split-reservations before and if there's a new integration issue

next_action.rationale: Root cause is now established as carrier-side issue (C9, inferred). Final diagnostic confirms: (1) whether carrier's pickup queue has EXC-0921 orders and their status, (2) any lag in carrier feed processing, (3) whether this is a known issue with split-reservation order handling. This will validate C9 and prepare for potential mitigation if carrier confirms the orders exist in their system but are stuck.
